howItWorks.title: How it works.
howItWorks.subtitle: Three steps: find a book, prepare it in your online library, send it to your e-reader.

find.title: Find a book
find.body: Search by title or author. Open-access sources on the platform, and local sources through the Gateway if you install it.

prepare.title: Prepare it in your library
prepare.body: Add the book to your online library. It is ready to send to your e-reader.

send.title: Send it to your e-reader
send.body: Choose the device. Ferry Agent handles the format and delivery.

mcpSpotlight.title: Your library, also from a conversation
mcpSpotlight.body: Search, add, and send your books from an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT…), with the same connection as the online workspace.

cloudFirst.q: Where are my books and settings?
cloudFirst.a: In Ferry Agent online: library, devices, settings, and delivery history are hosted on our infrastructure. Only the Gateway, if you install it, runs on your machine.

gatewayNeeded.q: Do I need the Gateway to get started?
gatewayNeeded.a: Not for open-access books (Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks) and your own uploaded files. The Gateway is for sources and downloads handled on your machine.

readers.a: Kindle (email delivery), Kobo and cloud-linked devices, Tolino and browsers via a temporary code, and any e-reader connected over USB.

myData.a: Yes. You manage your account, library, and devices. They are stored in Ferry Agent online; you can view and change them anytime.

agent.a: Yes. An AI assistant can search, add, and send for you, using the same connection as the workspace.

docs.metaDescription: Use Ferry Agent online, and install the Gateway at home only when you need it.
docs.title: Use Ferry Agent
docs.intro: Ferry Agent is an online app for your library and deliveries. The Gateway is an optional module installed on your machine, mainly for torrent downloads and your local sources.
docs.pathOnlineBody: Add books, manage devices, and follow deliveries without installing anything at home.
docs.pathGatewayBody: Useful only if you want to connect local sources or downloads handled on your machine.
docs.pathChoice: Recommended Gateway path: the Docker Desktop or OrbStack interface. Advanced options (terminal) are at the bottom of the page.
docs.checklistTitle: What you need for the Gateway
docs.checklistItem1: Docker Desktop installed (or OrbStack on Mac)
docs.checklistItem2: A Ferry Agent account, so you can open the Gateway page
docs.checklistItem3: The two codes shown only once at creation
docs.step1Action: Open the Gateway page, then click Add a Gateway. When it is created, note the connection code and the access key. Use the “Both codes together” block to copy everything at once — they will never be shown again.
docs.step1Success: Both codes appear once, with the “Both codes together” block.
docs.step2Action: Choose the file that matches your computer. It comes from an official Ferry Gateway release (same filename as in the release).
docs.step2DownloadIntro: Each file is an image ready to import into Docker Desktop or OrbStack (Docker format, one architecture per file).
docs.step2DownloadAmd64Hint: Windows, most Linux PCs, and Intel Macs.
docs.step2DownloadArm64Hint: Macs with Apple silicon (M1, M2, M3…).
docs.step2Unavailable: No Gateway release is linked to this guide yet.
docs.step2UnavailableHint: When a version is published, download buttons will appear here. Until then, open the releases page to check whether a file already exists.
docs.step2UseFile: After downloading, keep the file handy for the next step.
docs.step2Success: You have the install file that matches your computer.
docs.step3Title: Import the file in Docker Desktop or OrbStack
docs.step3Action: Open Docker Desktop or OrbStack. Import the downloaded .tar.gz file (Images → Import / Load), then wait until import finishes. This matches the release format: one Docker image per architecture.
docs.step3Success: The Gateway image appears in the Images list in Docker Desktop or OrbStack.
docs.step4Action: In Docker Desktop or OrbStack, start the imported image. Paste exactly the “Both codes together” block from Gateway (PAIRING_TOKEN and GATEWAY_KEY) into the startup settings that ask for them. Do not invent values, and do not leave blanks to fill in.
docs.step4Hint: Both codes are required. Without them, the Gateway page will stay waiting for a connection.
docs.step4Success: The module is running on your machine (started status in Docker Desktop or OrbStack).
docs.step5Action: Go back to the Gateway page in Ferry Agent. The status should become Connected.
docs.step5Success: On Gateway, the status shows Connected.
docs.afterBody: You can search for a book, add it to your online library, then send it to your e-reader. Local sources remain optional.
docs.afterMcp: For an AI assistant, add this address to Claude, ChatGPT, or your tool:
docs.closingLine: Find, prepare, send — your books follow this path to your e-reader.
docs.glossaryAccessDef: The module installed on your computer that links local sources and downloads to your online Ferry Agent library.
docs.glossaryCodesDef: Two distinct codes, shown only once at creation. The “Both codes together” block groups them so you can paste PAIRING_TOKEN and GATEWAY_KEY as-is.
docs.glossaryProwlarrDef: Local screen used with the Gateway to connect extra search sources at home. It is not the center of Ferry Agent navigation.
docs.glossaryIndexerDef: A site or catalog that lists books available to retrieve.
docs.troubleshootIntro: If something is stuck, start with these points:
docs.troubleshootWaiting: Gateway stays on “Waiting for the first connection”: check that the module is running in Docker Desktop or OrbStack, and that both codes are pasted there.
docs.troubleshootExpired: The code expired: on Gateway, click Create new codes, then update both codes in Docker Desktop or OrbStack.
docs.troubleshootOffline: Status Disconnected: restart the module at home. Your computer must stay on and connected to the internet. Your online library remains usable.
docs.troubleshootBothCodes: One code is not enough. Always paste the “Both codes together” block (connection code + access key).
docs.troubleshootProwlarr: To diagnose local sources (including Prowlarr), open the module’s local screen once Gateway is connected — often http://127.0.0.1:9696. This is not a page of the online library.
docs.terminalAltBody: If you prefer the terminal, start the already imported image and paste the real values from the “Both codes together” block (PAIRING_TOKEN and GATEWAY_KEY) as environment variables. Never replace them with sample values like CODE or KEY.
docs.terminalAltHint: Codes come only from the Gateway page, once at creation (or after Create new codes).
docs.byoDescription: Only the Gateway runs on your machine. Your library and settings stay in the online Ferry Agent app.
docs.byoBody1: Your computer must stay on and connected to the internet for Gateway searches and downloads to work.
docs.byoBody2: For continuous use, install the Gateway on a machine that stays on, using the same two codes.
